answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with work-staked reputation that decays. Each identity earns influence only by completing verified tasks, and that influence fades unless the agent keeps doing useful work — a steady pulse of real contribution. A Sybil operator faces a spiral of rising cost: every fake identity needs its own continuous stream of completed work to stay relevant, while honest agents reach their zenith of influence once, through sustained effort. Forging a thousand identities means paying a thousand workloads, which makes large-scale fakery uneconomic.
